wasm-vmDocsRoadmapOpen the machine

Linux in a browser tab.

wasm-vm is a RISC-V computer written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly. It boots an unmodified Linux kernel on your own device. There is nothing to install.

What the machine does

Browser APIs sit underneath. Linux sees a CPU, memory, interrupts and devices, as it would on hardware.

Runs real RISC-V binaries

Boot a kernel or run a bare-metal ELF. Privileged state, precise traps and virtual memory are part of the tested boundary.

CPU and platform →

Keeps a writable disk

Disk images are fetched in pieces as the guest reads them. A copy-on-write overlay in IndexedDB keeps your changes across reloads.

Disk and persistence →

Terminal or desktop

Use the serial terminal, or the Omarchy desktop with keyboard and pointer input. GPU rendering is used where the browser supports it; software rendering otherwise.

Display and input →

Shows what is proven

Guest traces, state digests and differential tests make execution inspectable. Each feature states its own limits.

Evidence and limits →

Try it on this page

A real BusyBox guest runs here; what you type goes to its shell. A few host status lines appear while it starts. Files, containers and the desktop are in the full app.

Measurements

File I/O, HTTP and steady-state compute timings for wasm-vm and other JavaScript runtimes. Every figure comes from a committed JSON file linked under its table; unsupported and unmeasured cells stay visible with their reason.

Scope. These are Node workload measurements from named environments, with their fixture, sampling policy, runtime identity and output checks. Methodology →

Measured, steady-state compute

Steady-state compute

This is a separate campaign from filesystem, stream, and HTTP boundaries. It keeps one process alive and times only deterministic arithmetic, branching, and typed-array loops.

Loading steady-state compute evidence…

Each measured cell shows median time, p95, and verified work rate. The fixture uses fixed checksums; process startup and memory preparation are excluded from timing. Measured browser rows come from the deployed Node guest; any remaining unmeasured row includes its reason. Runner · Raw compute comparison →
